openings.claim: Movement after the exception slip is completed may cause avoidable second searches. Evaluate a bounded probe that keeps retrieval and handoffs with the evening clerk and the existing shelves, cart, divider cards and paper slip; improved pickup performance remains unproven.
openings.delta: Investigate updating an existing exception entry when the clerk moves its book, instead of treating the pre-opening location as valid throughout the evening. Keep reader details behind the desk and preserve recipient verification before handoff.
openings.prediction: Second searches should concentrate among pickups whose exception entry became stale; contemporaneous updates should reduce those searches without requiring arrivals to leave the cart. The 95% within-two-minutes target and zero wrong-reader handoffs still require verification.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is household-surname misfiling: second searches should concentrate among mismatched shelf placements even when exception entries are current, so updating the slip alone would give little improvement. Peak demand could still prevent the timing target.
openings.defeat: The hypothesis is defeated if second searches show no association with stale exception entries and remain unchanged when entries accurately track moves, while household-name mismatches explain their locations.
openings.probe: Use the existing desk timing sheet behind the desk to tally stale-entry versus household-mismatch second searches and pickup duration. Trial move-time updates only within a measured total daily preparation budget of ten clerk-minutes, including later correction work. Stop added preparation at the cap; count a budget-limited trial as inconclusive. Record wrong-reader handoffs separately.
assumptions: Fit applies to the capped proposed probe, not a verified eventual intervention.
The eight-minute preparation sample does not establish spare capacity; the additional six correction minutes count against the ten-minute limit.
The clerk can observe location freshness and surname mismatch using existing hold information; that capability is unconfirmed.
All supplied observations are synthetic stipulations, not demonstrated benefits.
